content.title: Rory McIlroy net worth: How he makes and spends his money
content.text: Rory McIlroy is Nike's $200 million man — here's how he spends his millions and lives his life off the course Jamie Squire/Getty Images Aug 26, 2019, 2:25 PM UTC Rory McIlroy hasn't won a major since 2014, but his recent play suggests that could come to an end soon. His most recent payday was the largest in golf history — $15 million (€13 million) for winning the 2019 FedEx Cup. All of Rors' success on the course has led to a fantastic lifestyle off of the course. Visit BusinessInsider.com for more stories. Rory McIlroy has already built up quite a career. He has won three of the four major championships and four majors overall. He also has a deal with Nike rumored to be worth as much as $200 million (€180 million), as he was tasked, at the time, with replacing Tiger Woods as the face of Nike golf. He also has the makings of a pretty fantastic lifestyle off of the course, with a lavish house in Florida, a $400,000 (€360,000) car, and much more. Tony Manfred contributed to this report. McIlroy hasn't won a major since 2014, but he still earned close to $50 million (€45 million) on the course since the 2016 season between the PGA Tour and the European Tour. Stuart Franklin/Getty Images That included $10 million (€9 million) alone for winning the 2016 FedEx Cup. Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images He picked up another $15 million (€13 million) for winning the 2019 Fed Ex Cup, the largest payout in golf history. Keyur Khamar/PGA TOUR via Getty Images He also already ranks seventh on the career money list with nearly $70 million (€63 million) in tournament winnings. And that doesn't include his FedEx Cup winnings which are not counted towards the official money lists. John Bazemore/AP If the FedEx Cup winnings counted, McIlroy would already be third on the career money list, trailing only Tiger Woods and Phil Mickelson. McIlroy is only 30 years old. AP His official career earnings also don't include the millions he makes in appearance fees. In 2012, McIlroy raised his tournament appearance fee to $2 million (€1.8 million). It seems safe to assume that number is even higher now. Andrew Redington/Getty Images It is estimated that he makes $34 million (€31 million) a year in endorsements alone. Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images One recent estimate put McIlroy's net worth at approximately US$122 million (€110 million). But that was before his most recent FedEx Cup win. Stuart Franklin/Getty Images His biggest deal: a monster Nike contract rumored to be worth at least $200 million (€180 million). Nike Tiger Woods' first Nike deal was only worth $40 million (€36 million). Ross Kinnaird/Getty Images As the Nike Golf torch was seemingly passed from Woods to Rors, they did commercials together. Nike He also replaced Tiger on the cover of the EA Sports PGA Tour video game. EA Sports With all this money, he has been able to spend a little more on his haircuts. Ahmed Jadallah/Reuters Rory's other deals with Upper Deck, TaylorMade, and Omega make him golf's fourth-highest-paid player with $37.7 million (€33.9 million) in annual earnings. That trails only Tiger Woods, Phil Mickelson, and Jordan Spieth. YouTube/Omega The deal with TaylorMade is reportedly worth US$100 million (€90 million) over 10 years. TaylorMade He's not afraid to spend his money. He bought a gorgeous $9.5 million (€8.5 million) house in Florida in 2012. YouTube It was a pretty great bachelor pad. There's an incredible pool. YouTube And a game room. YouTube The house is good for his job, too. It's right next to the PGA National golf course and there's a workout room. YouTube Rory also put in a trophy room, with plenty of room for future hardware. YouTube The house he sold in Northern Ireland was being rented for $21,000 (€19,000) a week in 2014. Courtesy of Robinhall House He recently bought a house on Palm Jumeirah, the man-made island in Dubai, for an undisclosed amount. An aerial view of The Palm Island Jumeirah in Dubai and some residential homes that have been completed, November 8, 2007. REUTERS/Steve Crisp Steve Crisp/Reuters He was spotted driving a $400,000 (€360,000) Lamborghini Aventador. YouTube But in some ways, he is just like us. Instagram/Rory McIlroy After winning the PGA Championship, he took a private jet to New York to celebrate. @McIlroyRory The tabloids in the U.K. are all over him. They once reported that he bought a $2 million (€1.8 million) Bugatti, which he called "bollocks." REUTERS/Phil Noble Another tabloid fixation: his former relationship with tennis player Caroline Wozniacki. Matthew Lewis/Getty Images On New Year's Eve 2014, they got engaged. @CaroWozniacki But then, all of a sudden, he broke it off in May of 2014. They had already sent out wedding invitations. Getty Images Rory had his best season after the breakup in 2014, winning $1.7 million (€1.5 million) at the British Open and $1.8 million (€1.6 million) at the PGA Championship in 2014. REUTERS/Cathal McNaughton His dad won $170,000 (€153,000) too. When Rory was 15 his dad placed a bet that he would win the Open before he turned 25. @McIlroyRory Rory has also gotten into impeccable physical shape, putting on 20 pounds of muscle since 2010. @RoryMcIlroy Rory has since settled down with Erica Stoll Paul Childs/Reuters The pair got in some PDA prior to his first round at the 2017 Masters. ESPN They got married in 2017 at Ashford Castle in Ireland, a castle that has been referred to as the "most luxurious castle in the world." YouTube/Richard Bangs The wedding reportedly cost $260,000 (€234,000) and included a special performance from Stevie Wonder. Reuters Other attendees included Niall Horan from One Direction, actor Jamie Dornan, Ed Sheeran, and golfers Sergio Garcia, Shane Lowry and Paul McGinley. Andrew Redington/Getty Images The couple honeymooned at the Sandy Lane Hotel in Barbados, one of the most exclusive resorts in the world. YouTube/nathan wilson When he is not playing golf, he still knows his way around the soccer pitch. Instagram/Rory McIlroy McIlroy's golf game was quiet for a while after getting married, thanks to a nagging rib injury. But he was in near-peak form in 2019, with 14 top-10 finishes on the PGA Tour. Marianna Massey/Getty Images That included a win at The Players Championship that included a $2.3 million (€2.0 million) payday. Gerald Herbert/AP But McIlroy once said he has enough money now that he no longer cares about how much he wins. All he cares about now are wins, especially at the majors.
